title: SEMA Culture is a Vibe
summary: SEMA isn't just for industry buyers anymore. Here's why the Las Vegas show unites car enthusiasts of every style, and why it's still worth sore feet.
body_markdown:
Words & Photos by Ezekiel Wheeler


SEMA has been running since the late 1960s. A place where industry buyers and manufacturers could meet to discuss the latest product offerings and the special vehicles showcasing them.


Today, it’s a different story.


SEMA has become its own culture. Something beyond what you’re used to seeing at your local Cars & Coffee. It's a place where tribes of people descend on Las Vegas as if Mecca were calling, bringing their own style, flamboyance, flavors and energy to Sin City.


Want mullets, trucker hats, wraparound sunglasses and trucks taller than your single-story home? Yep, they’re at SEMA. Want your KITH jackets, clean sneakers and New York-style streetwear to pop in? Sure, you can find them at the Toyo Treadpass. Looking for all-out displacement and muscle machines of a bygone era? Central Hall has your New Balance- and cut-off-jort-wearing fans covered.


What strikes me every year isn’t the fact that different people attend. It’s that so many different people can celebrate one thing, and one thing universally. Even if they don't like your build, they respect the fact that you got a group of people together, built something and helped nudge the industry in a new direction. Right, wrong or indifferent, SEMA is for everyone who thrives on keeping car culture, technology, craftsmanship and fun alive and well for us all.


Hell, we saw a wedding take place in the CTEK booth for a few foreign influencers. Americans might scoff, but it reminds me that America is home to so many shows our friends across the pond dream of attending one day. So why not make the most of it when you get the opportunity to celebrate?


One exuberant individual I met while hunkering down at the XPEL booth in the West Hall was Dom. I was mid-conversation with a co-worker when Dom got me to snap my neck and leap from my chair. I ran over and asked, "How many have you acquired so far, amigo?!"


I was looking at the piles of lanyards draped around his neck. You couldn't even see skin, just sheer polyester and cotton, all branded.


> "I'm nearly up to 60!", Dom exclaimed.


"Here's another one, my friend. Thanks for stopping by, and I hope you reach 100!"


This! This is the excitement I'm looking for. The kind that keeps brands and co-workers like us excited to share in this unique world SEMA has created.


Yes, attendance, quality and caliber of the show shift as often as the tides. Some years are more epic than others. But we need to remember what makes this whole thing worthwhile: getting out to see the city, sharing a laugh at the booth, seeing a product knock your socks off, and witnessing people cherish a moment in time when we, as car enthusiasts, come together and truly celebrate each other.


Even if our feet are killing us by the end.
